alerts.title: Personal Income and Outlays, September 2026
alerts.summary: Personal income increased $54.5 billion (0.2 percent at a monthly rate) in September, according to estimates released today by the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA). Disposable personal income (DPI)–personal income less personal current taxes–increased $52.7 billion (0.2 percent), and personal consumption expenditures (PCE) increased $113.1 billion (0.5 percent). Personal outlays–the sum of PCE, personal interest payments, and personal current transfer payments–increased $113.0 billion in September. Personal saving was $911.1 billion, and the personal saving rate–personal saving as a percentage of DPI–was 3.8 percent.

alerts.title: U.S. International Trade in Goods and Services, September 2026
alerts.summary: The U.S. goods and services trade deficit decreased in September 2026 according to the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis and the U.S. Census Bureau. The deficit decreased from $105.7 billion in August (revised) to $105.0 billion in September, as exports increased more than imports. The goods deficit decreased $0.7 billion in September to $135.9 billion. The services surplus decreased less than $0.1 billion in September to $30.9 billion.

alerts.title: GDP (Advance Estimate), 3rd Quarter 2026
alerts.summary: Real gross domestic product (GDP) increased at an annual rate of 3.4 percent in the third quarter of 2026 (July, August, and September), according to the advance estimate released today by the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA). In the second quarter, real GDP increased 2.2 percent. The contributors to the increase in real GDP in the third quarter were increases in investment, consumer spending, and government spending that were partly offset by a decrease in exports. Imports, which are a subtraction in the calculation of GDP, increased.
